claims.text: Standard uniaxial tensile testing can reliably characterize the mechanical properties of FeNiCrMn HEAs.
Yield strength, ultimate tensile strength, and ductility of FeNiCrMn HEAs can be obtained from uniaxial tensile testing.
The proposed specimens are FeNiCrMn HEAs in either an as-cast or solution-treated state.
The alloy will be subjected to uniaxial tensile loading at controlled strain rates and temperatures.
Testing will span ambient to moderately elevated temperatures under controlled strain rates.
Grain size affects the deformation behavior of FeNiCrMn HEAs.
Phase distribution and defect density affect the deformation behavior of FeNiCrMn HEAs.
Grain boundaries and phase interfaces mediate dislocation motion during tensile loading.
Grain boundaries and phase interfaces influence crack initiation during tensile loading.
Microstructure-mediated dislocation motion and crack initiation determine the observed tensile response.
Tensile testing will reveal a quantifiable strength–ductility trade-off in FeNiCrMn HEAs.
Tensile results can provide a basis for correlating microstructure with mechanical performance.
Existing FeNiCrMn HEA studies have primarily characterized corrosion resistance and have not provided detailed mechanical-property evaluation.
Uniaxial tensile testing probes bulk macroscopic mechanical response but may not resolve local strain heterogeneity.
Processing history and specimen preparation can introduce variability into tensile measurements.
Heat treatments can be used to produce controlled differences in grain size for the proposed comparison.
